name: Increased memory limit
plain: Raises the foreground memory cap for heavy apps.
meaning: No privacy impact; shows how OS gives bigger resource caps to apps that ask in a manifest or entitlement.

ios.note: Raises per process limit on supported devices

limits.headline: Can ask for more working memory for heavy tasks, with no prompt
limits.user_action: Nothing. The developer turns this on before the app ships
can: Raise the app's memory cap on supported iPhones
Ask for a large memory heap on Android with one setting
Open big photos, video or maps without running out of memory
cannot: Go past what your phone physically has
Get approval on Android; it needs none, but it is only a request
Gain extra access to your data
Keep apps from being closed when memory is low for the whole system
limits.differs: On Android it is a manifest setting needing no approval. On iPhone it is an Apple capability that works on supported devices.

story.what_it_is: A setting that lets heavy apps use more memory while on screen.

marketing.name: Increased Memory Limit entitlement
marketing.pitch: Developer rule: apps that need more memory, such as big games or editors, can ask for a higher limit.

story.for_you: You will never see it. It only helps demanding apps like large games, video editors or maps keep running instead of closing without warning.
story.for_makers: Makers ask for it when a normal memory cap makes their app crash. On Android a similar flag asks for a larger heap. It does not collect data about you.

use_cases.example: A big open world game asks for more memory so it does not close in the middle of a boss fight.
A video or photo editor keeps a long project in memory without crashing.
An AR app holds a 3D scan of your room in memory while you walk around.
A map app keeps large map tiles in memory for smooth zooming.
A developer who sees the app killed for using too much memory turns this on after other fixes.

story.android_note: Apps ask for a large heap in their manifest, and the system may still limit them.
story.ios_note: Needs an entitlement in the app, and only some devices honor it.
